title: Rook and Bishop against Rook and Knight
subtitle: Keep your pieces free while restricting the opponent

source.author: José Raúl Capablanca
source.section: Chapter V, §30 Rook, Bishop and Pawns v. Rook, Knight and Pawns, Example 62

narration.say: We follow the first game of the Lasker–Marshall championship match of 1907. Opening phase 1.
We follow the first game of the Lasker–Marshall championship match of 1907. Opening phase 2.
We follow the first game of the Lasker–Marshall championship match of 1907. Opening phase 3.
We follow the first game of the Lasker–Marshall championship match of 1907. Opening phase 4.

steps.title: Black has the more active pieces

narration.say: White’s rook and knight are still on their original squares. Black can exploit that delay.
The rook attacks b2 and provokes a pawn move.
Now the rook can change wings.

exercise.prompt: Black to move. Lift the rook to the fifth rank.

narration.say: Black attacks the kingside pawns. White brings the king back, and Black advances c5.
White develops the knight, but its own pawns limit its routes. Black activates the king.
White checks with the rook. Black goes where the king wanted to go anyway.
White plays a3. Black prepares another transfer.
The bishop can restrict the knight and support the kingside blockade.

exercise.prompt: Black to move. Develop the bishop to g4.

narration.say: Black centralises the king while White advances a4.
White retreats the king. Black’s rook changes wings again.
Black advances the passed pawn and invades with the king.

steps.title: Exchange rooks without releasing the pressure

narration.say: White exchanges rooks. Black recaptures and retains the active king and bishop.
Black uses pawn moves to make White move the knight or king.
The bishop and king penetrate further.

steps.title: Create threats the knight cannot meet

narration.say: White attacks queenside pawns, but Black advances f4 and f3.
Black creates another passed pawn on the queenside.
White resigns. The knight cannot cope with Black’s widely separated threats.

steps.title: Activity determines the value of the pieces

narration.say: Black kept the rook mobile, made White defend pawns, and activated the king.
After the rook exchange, the bishop and king kept restricting the knight. Passed pawns then decided the game.
